edges.mechanism: Methotrexate is a DHFR inhibitor that competes with reduced folates for cellular transport; folate products may reduce its efficacy in neoplastic disease, whereas folic/folinic acid is directed in RA/psoriasis/pJIA to cut toxicity.
edges.evidence: FDA label; Cochrane review in RA (transaminase elevation RR 0.23, withdrawal RR 0.39, efficacy preserved); no 5-MTHF-specific trial

edges.mechanism: Reduced folate stabilizes the FdUMP-thymidylate synthase complex, increasing fluorouracil effect and toxicity; label instructs avoiding folic acid/folate-analog products unless directed.
edges.evidence: FDA label; prospective CRC cohort: folic acid supplement use HR 1.81 for toxicity

edges.mechanism: Same thymidylate-synthase mechanism as capecitabine (its prodrug): folates potentiate fluorouracil toxicity; fatal enterocolitis reported with leucovorin plus weekly 5-FU in elderly patients.
edges.evidence: FDA capecitabine label drug-interaction section

edges.mechanism: Phenytoin lowers folate; folate supplementation can increase phenytoin metabolism and lower serum levels (breakthrough seizures), and alters time to steady state.
edges.evidence: Pharmacokinetic studies and review; medical-food label

edges.mechanism: Enzyme-inducing antiepileptics lower serum folate; supplementation is used to correct deficiency.
edges.evidence: Cross-sectional comparison (carbamazepine, phenobarbital vs valproate); scoping review; label

edges.mechanism: Teratogenic antifolate-related NTD risk; guidelines advise avoiding valproate in people who could become pregnant and >=0.4 mg/day folic acid with any antiseizure drug, though folic acid did not lower malformation risk in a meta-analysis of women with epilepsy.
edges.evidence: AAN/AES/SMFM 2024 guideline; AAN 2009 practice parameter; observational SR

edges.mechanism: Inhibits intestinal folate absorption, predisposing to folate deficiency.
edges.evidence: Clinical absorption study in ulcerative colitis

edges.mechanism: Weak DHFR inhibitor; 400 mg/day for 7 days lowered serum folate vs placebo.
edges.evidence: RCT in healthy volunteers

edges.mechanism: Antifolate (DHFR inhibitor) affecting human folate metabolism; high-dose folic acid may antagonize antimalarial antifolate efficacy, whereas 5-MTHF bypasses DHFR and is proposed as non-antagonizing.
edges.evidence: Clinical metabolic study; review of malaria-in-pregnancy data

edges.mechanism: Long-term metformin lowers vitamin B12 and raises homocysteine; label lists decreased serum folate. Folate may then mask emerging B12 deficiency.
edges.evidence: 4-year RCT (B12); medical-food label

edges.mechanism: L-methylfolate 15 mg/day augments antidepressant response (proposed via monoamine synthesis/methylation).
edges.evidence: SR/MA (response RR 1.25, SMD -0.38) and sequential RCTs; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Methionine synthase requires B12 to demethylate 5-MTHF; without B12, folate is trapped as 5-MTHF. Co-supplementation is recommended to avoid masking deficiency.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic review; narrative clinical review; homocysteine NMA

edges.mechanism: Combined methylfolate plus methylcobalamin lowers homocysteine via methionine synthase.
edges.evidence: Hemodialysis RCT (800 ug + 1000 ug, 3 months); genotype-stratified RCT with P5P

edges.mechanism: Folate plus B6 and B12 combinations lower homocysteine more than single agents.
edges.evidence: Network MA of RCTs in healthy adults

edges.mechanism: Pyridoxal-5-phosphate supports transsulfuration of homocysteine; combined with methylfolate and methylcobalamin it lowered homocysteine.
edges.evidence: RCT (methylfolate+P5P+methylcobalamin); NMA

edges.mechanism: Riboflavin (FAD) is the MTHFR cofactor; supplementation raises SAM and modifies BP in MTHFR 677TT carriers.
edges.evidence: RCT metabolite analysis; JINGO cohort analysis

edges.mechanism: Betaine remethylates homocysteine through BHMT, independently of folate/B12; additive with low-dose B vitamins.
edges.evidence: MA of 5 RCTs (-1.23 umol/L at >=4 g/d); RCT with B vitamins plus betaine

edges.mechanism: High folate corrects the megaloblastic anemia while neurological damage progresses; high folate with low B12 is linked to anemia, cognitive impairment and worse MMA/homocysteine. Higher 5-MTHF was also linked to anemia in low-B12 seniors.
edges.evidence: NHANES analyses; clinical reviews; medical-food label

edges.mechanism: 1 mg/day folic acid increased advanced/multiple adenomas and sessile serrated lesions in an RCT; pooled trials null; relevance to 5-MTHF unknown.
edges.evidence: RCT and long-term follow-up; pooled RCTs

edges.mechanism: Label warns of possible mood elevation when used in depression in patients at risk of bipolar disorder.
edges.evidence: Medical-food label; small open registry

edges.mechanism: TT genotype lowers folate response to folic acid and raises homocysteine at low folate; 5-MTHF bypasses MTHFR, but genotype-guided benefit is unproven and ACMG advises against routine testing.
edges.evidence: MA of intervention studies; RCTs; ACMG guideline

edges.mechanism: Supplementation causes true rises; serum folate reflects recent intake, RBC folate about 4 months; immunoassay and microbiological values are not interchangeable; 5-MTHF degrades in stored samples.
edges.evidence: Laboratory review; method comparison; trial report
